concept_definition: A domesticated canine animal (Canis familiaris) kept as a pet, for companionship, or for work such as guarding or herding.
A small domesticated carnivorous mammal kept as a pet or for catching mice, typically with soft fur, a short snout, and retractile claws.
A warm-blooded, egg-laying vertebrate with feathers, wings, and usually the ability to fly; members of class Aves.
A large domesticated mammal with a mane and tail, used for riding, racing, or pulling loads.
A domesticated bovine animal (Bos taurus), used here as the common everyday term regardless of sex.
A domesticated hoofed mammal raised for meat (pork) and other products; typically Sus scrofa domesticus.
a domesticated fowl (Gallus gallus domesticus) kept for its eggs and meat; an adult female is specifically called a hen
A small rodent with a pointed snout, rounded ears, and a long tail, typically living in or near human dwellings.
A large mammal with a thick fur coat, a bulky body, and a short tail, living in forests or mountains. Bears are omnivores and may hibernate in winter.
a large carnivorous mammal (Canis lupus) of the dog family, typically living and hunting in packs and found in wild habitats across the Northern Hemisphere
A small mammal with long ears, soft fur, and a short tail, often kept as a pet or found in the wild.
A large marine mammal that lives in the ocean and is known for its size and singing sounds.
A large wild cat with orange fur and black stripes, known for its strength and agility.
A snake is a long, legless reptile that moves by slithering and often has scales.
A very large gray mammal with a long trunk and tusks; native to Africa and Asia.
A large sea fish with a skeleton made of cartilage; a predator known for its sharp teeth.
A nocturnal bird of prey with a flat face and large forward-facing eyes, known for hunting at night and often symbolizing wisdom.
A small arthropod with eight legs that often spins webs to catch insects.
A small to medium-sized rodent with a bushy tail, typically living in trees and feeding on nuts and seeds.
A small to medium-sized hoofed mammal (Capra aegagrus hircus) kept for milk, meat, fiber, or as a domestic farm animal.
A large waterfowl with a long neck, webbed feet, and a flat bill, commonly kept domestically or found wild (singular).
A waterbird with a broad body, short legs, a flat bill, and webbed feet, commonly found in ponds, lakes, and rivers.
A small tailless amphibian with a short body, long hind legs for jumping, smooth moist skin, and bulging eyes, typically living near water.
A flying insect with two pairs of large, often colorful wings and a slender body; undergoes metamorphosis from caterpillar to adult.
A reptile with a hard shell covering its body, typically living in water or on land and able to retract its head and legs into its shell.

A medium- to large-sized passerine bird of the genus Corvus, with glossy black plumage, a strong stout bill, and a loud harsh "caw" call; known for high intelligence and adaptable omnivorous feeding habits.
A large bird of prey with a hooked beak and strong talons, known for keen eyesight and powerful flight.
A domesticated, woolly mammal kept by humans for its wool, meat, and milk; refers to an individual of the species (Ovis aries).
a living organism that feeds on organic matter
a living being, especially an animal
a large wild animal
A cold-blooded aquatic vertebrate that typically has gills, fins, and scales; refers to the living creature.
A large wild cat with a tawny coat and, in the male, a flowing mane; native to Africa and parts of Asia.
A small to medium-sized primate typically having a long tail, living in trees in tropical regions.
A hoofed grazing mammal with branched antlers in the male, found in forests and grasslands worldwide.
A small to medium-sized wild canine with a pointed muzzle, bushy tail, and reddish fur, known for cunning.
A flying insect known for producing honey and beeswax, and for pollinating flowers.
A small social insect living in organized colonies, known for strength and industriousness.
A highly intelligent marine mammal with a streamlined body and a beak-like snout, known for playful behavior.
A flightless seabird of the Southern Hemisphere with black and white plumage and flipper-like wings for swimming.
A tall African mammal with a very long neck and legs, and a distinctive spotted coat pattern.
An African wild horse with black and white stripes, living in herds on grasslands.
A large semiaquatic reptile with a long snout, powerful jaws, and a thick scaly hide, found in tropical regions.
A domesticated hoofed mammal related to the horse, with long ears and a braying call, used as a beast of burden.
A medium-sized rodent with a pointed snout and a long scaly tail, larger than a mouse.
A tropical bird with a curved beak and brightly colored plumage, often able to mimic human speech.
A stout-bodied bird with a small head, commonly found in urban areas worldwide.
A nocturnal flying mammal with membranous wings, using echolocation to navigate.
A large long-necked mammal with one or two humps, adapted to desert life and used for transport.
A large, powerful ape with dark fur that lives in the forests of central Africa.
A large semiaquatic African mammal with thick skin that spends much of its time in water.
A large herbivorous mammal with thick skin and one or two horns on its snout, native to Africa and Asia.
A large wild cat with a yellowish-brown coat marked with dark rosette-shaped spots.
A large Australian marsupial with powerful hind legs for jumping and a long tail for balance.
A soft-bodied sea creature with eight long tentacles, known for its intelligence and ability to change color.
A small flying insect that bites and sucks blood from humans and animals.
A small creature with a soft body and a spiral shell on its back, moving very slowly.
A small animal with a long, thin, soft body and no legs or bones.
An adult male chicken, known for crowing at dawn.
A large waterbird with a long graceful neck, typically having white plumage.
A large bird, the male of which has very long colorful tail feathers that can spread like a fan.
A tall wading bird with pink or reddish plumage, long legs, and a curved beak.
A large black-and-white bear native to the mountain forests of central China.
A crustacean with a broad shell, stalked eyes, and five pairs of legs, the front pair bearing large pincers.
A large marine crustacean with a hard exoskeleton, large front claws, and a segmented tail.
a domesticated bird such as a chicken, turkey, or duck, kept for eggs or meat.
a small arthropod animal with six legs and typically one or two pairs of wings.
a large white bear of the Arctic
a small tailless rodent kept as a pet
a large white-headed North American eagle
a large black and white toothed whale
a bee that produces honey and lives in colonies

lt.translation_status_note: Compound used to specify the honey-producing species; the short form bitė is too general.

concept_definition: a venomous American snake with a rattling tail
a large tawny wild cat of the Americas
a large eared seal of coastal waters

lt.translation_status_note: Common descriptive compound; no fully idiomatic single native term.

concept_definition: An animal that is hunted and killed by another animal for food.
A usually nocturnal flying insect related to butterflies, typically with a stout body and wings covered in tiny scales; some species damage clothing or stored food.
An insect with a hard shell-like pair of wing covers, usually four wings, and chewing mouthparts.
A large wild ox native to Africa, especially the African buffalo.
An animal that hunts, kills, and eats other animals.
A freshwater or sea-dwelling fish of the salmon family, commonly caught for food or sport; the plural can also be trout.
A fast-running, long-eared mammal related to the rabbit, typically living in open country and giving birth to young that are born with fur and open eyes.
A large deer with broad, flattened antlers, native to northern forests of North America, Europe, and Asia.
A large black bird of the crow family, known for its intelligence and harsh call.
A bird of prey with long, pointed wings and a forked tail, often seen soaring while searching for food.
The feathers covering a bird’s body, especially considered as a whole or in terms of their color and pattern.
An insect, animal, or plant that harms crops, livestock, property, or human health.
A large, hump-backed wild bovine mammal with a shaggy coat, especially the American bison or the European bison.
An animal of the class Mammalia, characterized generally by having hair or fur, warm blood, and females that produce milk to feed their young.
An animal with a backbone or spinal column, including mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
An eel-like marine animal that produces copious slime when threatened and is considered a primitive jawless fish.
A freshwater or marine fish with whisker-like barbels around its mouth, belonging to the order Siluriformes.
A small freshwater crustacean resembling a miniature lobster, with a segmented body and large claws.
Any of several freshwater fish that can breathe air with one or two lung-like organs, allowing them to survive periods when their habitat dries out.
A semiaquatic Australian mammal with a broad bill, webbed feet, dense fur, and a beaver-like tail; one of the few mammals that lays eggs.
An organism that lives on or in another organism and obtains nourishment or other benefits from it, usually harming the host.
A large, flat marine fish of the flounder family, prized as food and found mainly in northern oceans.
A small, slender marine fish of the herring family, often preserved in salt or oil and used as food.
A marine or freshwater mollusk with a soft body enclosed in two hinged shells; also, its edible flesh.
A cod, especially one used as food; the flesh of a cod used as food.
A soft-bodied marine animal with a bell-shaped, jellylike body and trailing tentacles, often capable of delivering a sting.
A scaly, usually four-legged reptile with a long tail, movable eyelids, and no shell; lizards include many different species.
A domesticated animal kept for companionship or pleasure rather than for work or food.
A flightless bird native to New Zealand, with a long slender bill and hairlike feathers.
A small blood-feeding arachnid that attaches to animals or people.
A young cat, especially one not yet fully grown.
A young dog, especially one that is not yet fully grown.
An extinct reptile of a diverse group that lived mainly during the Mesozoic Era.
A land-dwelling reptile with a hard shell, short legs, and a generally slow-moving nature.
The leading or dominant individual in a social group of animals.
A bass is a fish of a group that includes several freshwater and marine species, many of which are popular as game fish.
An animal that moves seasonally or periodically from one region to another.
A person, animal, or organism that carries and can transmit a disease or infectious agent, often without being affected by it.
A broiler chicken is a young chicken raised primarily for its meat.
An immature form of an insect or other animal that undergoes metamorphosis.
A gull is a seabird, commonly found near coasts and waterways, with long wings and webbed feet.
A female red deer, especially one that is fully grown.
An animal with which another animal mates to reproduce.
An adult male bovine, especially one kept for breeding on a farm.
A castrated male bovine trained to pull loads or work in farming.
A young bovine animal raised in farming, whether male or female.
A young female bovine that has not yet given birth to a calf.
An adult female chicken kept or raised on a farm, especially for producing eggs.
A young sheep, especially one that is less than a year old.
An adult male sheep kept or raised in farming, especially for breeding.
An adult female sheep kept or bred in farming, especially for producing lambs or wool.
A young pig, especially one that is still nursing or has not yet been weaned.
A young horse, especially one that is still dependent on its mother.
Farm animals kept for meat, milk, wool, or work.
Domestic birds such as chickens, ducks, geese, and turkeys that are kept or raised on a farm.
A young castrated male bovine raised for beef.
A young castrated male bovine raised or kept on a farm.
An adult female pig kept or used for breeding on a farm.
An uncastrated male pig kept for breeding on a farm.
An uncastrated adult male horse used or kept in farming, including for breeding or work.
An adult female horse kept or used in farming.
A young goat raised or kept on a farm.
A male horse that has been castrated, especially one kept or used on a farm.
A young male horse, especially one that has not been castrated.
A young female horse, especially one being raised or kept on a farm.
A young female pig that has not yet had piglets.
A male duck, especially one kept or raised on a farm.
A male goose kept or raised in farming.
A young female chicken, especially one that has not yet begun laying eggs.
A young male chicken raised or kept in farming before it reaches adulthood.
A dog trained to herd and manage sheep on a farm.
The woolly coat shorn from a sheep in farming.
A wooden enclosure used on a farm to house rabbits.
A curved metal plate, usually iron, nailed to a horse’s hoof to protect it while working on a farm.
A marine bivalve mollusk with a rough, irregular shell, eaten as food; some kinds produce pearls.
A small, fast-flying bird with long pointed wings and a forked tail, belonging to the family Hirundinidae.
A bright red North American songbird, especially the male of the northern cardinal, which has a crest and a thick bill.
A snake, especially one regarded as large, dangerous, or symbolically significant.
The dead body of an animal, especially one used for food or left after being killed.
A bird of prey with broad wings, a hooked beak, and sharp talons, often seen hunting small animals.
A pig, especially a domesticated pig raised for meat.
A dog bred or used for hunting, especially one that tracks game by scent.
A large marine fish with a mild-flavored white flesh, especially one of the fishes of the family Gadidae; also, its flesh used as food.
A marine animal that lives in colonies of tiny polyps, often forming hard branching or rounded structures from calcium carbonate.
A large, long-legged, long-necked wading bird.
An organism in an early stage of development, before it has the form of a fetus in mammals or before it hatches or becomes independent in other organisms.
A small, silvery marine fish that lives in large schools in the North Atlantic and North Pacific and is often eaten or preserved.
Domesticated bovines, especially adult cattle, kept or trained as draft animals; the term is the plural of ox.
A freshwater fish, especially one of the family Percidae, including the European perch and yellow perch.
A bird of the pigeon family, especially one regarded as a symbol of peace or gentleness.
A small, short-tailed game bird, several kinds of which are found in different parts of the world.
A small seed-eating bird, especially a common brown or gray songbird of the family Passeridae.
An organism, especially an insect or other animal, that carries and transmits a pathogen or parasite between hosts.
A person or animal saved from danger or taken into care, especially an animal adopted from a shelter or a rescue organization.
A large primate without a tail, including chimpanzees, gorillas, orangutans, and gibbons; often contrasted with monkeys.
A small insect or similar small creature, especially one regarded as a pest.
A sturdy hybrid animal produced by crossing a male donkey with a female horse, typically sterile and used for carrying loads or riding.
Animals and other living organisms that live and grow in natural conditions, especially away from human care or cultivation.
An unborn offspring of a human or other mammal during the later stages of development; in humans, the stage from the end of the eighth week after fertilization until birth.
An organism produced by crossing individuals of different species, varieties, or breeds.
A male deer, especially an adult male deer of certain species.
An adult male chicken, especially one kept for breeding; a rooster.
A small horse, especially one of a breed that remains small when fully grown.
An animal hunted or pursued, especially by hunters or birds of prey.
An animal, especially a domestic one, that has wandered away from its home or owner.
A marine mammal with flippers and a streamlined body, adapted for swimming and often living in cold seas.
A large semiaquatic rodent known for its broad, flat tail and for building dams across rivers.
A semiaquatic mammal in the family Mustelidae, with thick fur and webbed feet, that swims in rivers and often eats fish.
A small mammal covered in stiff spines that can curl into a ball for protection.
A North American mammal in the genus Procyon, known for its gray fur, black facial mask, and ringed tail.
A spotted big cat (Acinonyx jubatus) known as the fastest land animal.
An Australian tree-dwelling marsupial that feeds mainly on eucalyptus leaves.
A small rodent in the family Cricetidae, characterized by cheek pouches and often kept as a pet.
A deer of the far north, known for its large antlers and often used to pull sledges.
A black-and-white mammal in the family Mephitidae that can spray a foul-smelling liquid from glands near its tail.
A stout, grey burrowing mammal with a distinctive black-and-white striped face.
An African great ape of the genus *Pan*, one of the closest living relatives of humans.
A carnivorous mammal in the family Hyaenidae, especially an African species known for its doglike appearance and distinctive laughing call.
A large spotted big cat native to Central and South America, known scientifically as Panthera onca.
A domesticated South American camelid with a woolly coat, used as a pack animal and for its fiber.
A large Arctic marine mammal of the seal family, known for its long tusks.
A fast, slender, horned grazing mammal, especially one native to Africa or Asia.
A rodent covered in long, sharp quills.
A small burrowing mammal with dark fur and tiny eyes.
A tree-dwelling tropical mammal that moves slowly and often hangs upside down from branches.
A medium-sized wild cat in the genus Lynx, characterized by tufted ears and a short tail.
A very large African bird that cannot fly and runs fast.
A small songbird with a red-orange breast, especially a member of the thrush family in the genus *Erithacus* or *Turdus*.
A large gallinaceous bird raised for its meat and often eaten at festive meals.
A large water bird of the family Pelecanidae, with a long bill and a pouch beneath it used to catch fish.
A bird in the family Picidae that uses its strong bill to peck holes in tree trunks, often to find food or make a nest.
A large scavenging bird, usually with a bare head, that feeds mainly on the carcasses of dead animals.
A falcon is a fast-flying bird of prey with long, pointed wings, belonging to the family Falconidae.
A small songbird in the finch family, often yellow and kept as a pet.
A small bird in the family Trochilidae that can hover while feeding on nectar from flowers.
A large wading bird in the family Ciconiidae, typically tall with long legs and a long red beak.
In zoology, a fly is an insect of the order Diptera, typically with one pair of functional wings, such as a housefly.
A flying insect in the order Hymenoptera, often yellow and black, that can sting.
In zoology, a caterpillar is the long, soft larval stage of a butterfly or moth.
A small, round beetle, usually red with black spots, in the family Coccinellidae.
In zoology, a grasshopper is an insect with long hind legs adapted for jumping, often producing chirping sounds by rubbing its body parts together.
A predatory insect in the order Odonata, with a long, slender body and two pairs of clear, often brightly patterned wings.
A brown, flat-bodied insect in the order Blattodea, often found in buildings and able to thrive in unhygienic conditions.
A small, wingless, jumping insect in the order Siphonaptera that feeds on the blood of animals and can bite people.
An amphibian, usually with dry, bumpy skin and shorter hind legs than a frog, belonging to a group commonly called toads.
The aquatic larval stage of a frog or toad, which has a tail and develops into an adult amphibian.
A large semiaquatic reptile in the family Alligatoridae, similar to a crocodile but typically with a broader, U-shaped snout.
A venomous snake in the family Elapidae that can flatten the skin of its neck into a hood when threatened.
A large, nonvenomous constricting snake in the family Pythonidae that kills its prey by squeezing it.
A lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae, known for its ability to change the color of its skin.
A long, slender, snakelike fish belonging to the order Anguilliformes.
A small orange freshwater fish, Carassius auratus, often kept as a pet in an aquarium or bowl.
A small marine fish in the genus Hippocampus that swims upright and has a head resembling a horse’s.
A marine animal in the class Asteroidea, typically with a central body and five radiating arms.
A marine mollusk with an elongated body, a pair of longer tentacles, and eight shorter arms.
A shell-less or reduced-shell gastropod mollusk that moves on a muscular foot and produces mucus.
An arachnid with pincers and a segmented tail ending in a venomous sting.
A long, flattened, many-legged arthropod in the class Chilopoda, whose body has one pair of legs on each segment.
A soil-dwelling annelid worm that burrows through the ground and feeds on decaying organic matter.
An American mammal with a body covered in bony armor plates.
A Central or South American mammal with a long snout that feeds mainly on ants and termites.
A large African monkey of the genus Papio, with a long, doglike muzzle.
A small, striped ground squirrel of the genus Tamias or a closely related genus.
A wild canine native to North America that is smaller than a wolf.
A very large deer of the genus Cervus, especially the wapiti of North America or the red deer called an elk in Europe.
A small domesticated mammal related to the weasel, commonly kept as a pet or used for hunting small animals.
A small, graceful antelope native to Africa and Asia.
A small desert-dwelling rodent in the subfamily Gerbillinae, sometimes kept as a pet.
A tree-dwelling primate with a long tail, native only to Madagascar.
A domesticated South American camelid, smaller than a llama, raised mainly for its fine wool.
A small African mongoose that often stands upright to watch for predators and other danger.
A small carnivorous mammal of Africa and Asia, known for preying on snakes.
A large, long-armed, red-haired ape native to the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra.
A large cat with a black coat, especially a leopard with melanism, in zoology.
A small toothed whale in the family Phocoenidae, typically with a blunt snout.
A small, slender carnivorous mammal in the mustelid family, typically with brown fur, that hunts small animals.
A large, powerful mammal of northern forests in the weasel family, known for its strength and fierce behavior.
A large, long-haired bovine of the Himalayan region, kept as a domesticated animal or found in the wild.
A burrowing Australian marsupial with a stout body and short legs.
A small or medium-sized Australian marsupial in the kangaroo family.
A blue whale is a very large baleen whale and the largest animal known to have ever lived on Earth.
A marine mammal of the North Pacific that often floats on its back, using its chest to hold food while feeding.
A wild canine of Africa and Asia, often a scavenger that feeds on carrion.
A wild pig native to forests across Europe and Asia, scientifically known as Sus scrofa.
A songbird of the thrush family, especially the Eurasian blackbird (Turdus merula), whose male has black plumage and a yellow beak.
A bird in the cuckoo family that lays its eggs in the nests of other bird species, which then raise its young.
A small seed-eating songbird in the family Fringillidae, typically with a short, thick beak.
A tall wading bird in the family Ardeidae, typically with long legs and a long neck.
A small, brightly colored bird in the family Alcedinidae that often dives into water to catch fish.
A black-and-white bird of the crow family, known for its long tail.
A small brown songbird of the genus Luscinia, famous for its rich song, especially at night.
A game bird in the family Phasianidae, especially one whose male has a long tail and brightly colored feathers.
A seabird in the genus *Fratercula*, known for its black-and-white plumage and large, brightly colored beak.
A tropical American bird in the family Ramphastidae, known for its enormous, brightly colored bill.
A large, flightless bird native to Australia, belonging to the genus Dromaius.
A wren is a tiny brown songbird, typically with a short, upright tail.
A large, brightly coloured parrot native to Central and South America.
A very large vulture native to South America, especially the Andean condor.
A large tropical American lizard, especially one of the genus *Iguana*, with a crest of spines along its back.
A small lizard in the infraorder Gekkota, often able to climb walls using specialized toe pads.
A venomous snake in the family Viperidae, typically with long, hinged fangs that inject venom.
A very large South American snake, especially one of the genus *Eunectes*, that lives in or near water.
A salamander is a smooth-skinned amphibian with a long body and tail that resembles a lizard.
A small salamander in the family Salamandridae that typically lives both in water and on land.
A small marine fish in the herring family, commonly found in schools and often used as food.
A marine fish of the genus *Scomber*, known for its blue-green back marked with dark stripes.
A large freshwater fish of the family Cyprinidae, often raised in ponds for food or sport.
A large ocean fish in the billfish family, known for its long, flat, swordlike snout.
A flat-bodied cartilaginous fish with a venomous spine on its tail.
A small South American freshwater fish with sharp teeth, belonging to the family Serrasalmidae.
A small orange-and-white marine fish that lives among sea anemones.
A large social wasp in the genus *Vespa*, often nesting in trees or buildings.
A large, hairy bee of the genus *Bombus*, known for its robust body and often brightly banded coloring.
A cricket is a jumping insect that produces a chirping sound, often at night.
In zoology, a grasshopper that can form large migrating swarms and devastate crops.
A social insect in the order Blattodea that lives in colonies and feeds mainly on wood or other plant material.
A beetle that produces light at night, especially one in the family Lampyridae.
A predatory insect in the order Mantodea, known for holding its enlarged front legs together as if praying.
A large, hairy spider, especially one belonging to the family Theraphosidae.
A marine decapod crustacean resembling a large shrimp, with a long body and slender legs.
A marine or freshwater bivalve mollusk with an elongated shell, often dark blue-black, that lives attached to surfaces or partly buried in sediment.
A segmented aquatic or terrestrial worm in the class Hirudinea, many species of which attach to animals and suck their blood.
A long, crawling arthropod in the class Diplopoda, usually with many legs and two pairs of legs on most body segments.
A round marine animal in the class Echinoidea, typically covered in movable spines.
A vertebrate animal in the zoological group Reptilia, typically cold-blooded and covered with scales, such as a snake, lizard, or turtle.
A cold-blooded vertebrate in zoology that typically lives in water during its early life and on land as an adult.
A mammal in the zoological order Rodentia, characterized by a single pair of continuously growing, chisel-like incisors in each jaw that it uses for gnawing.
A mammal belonging to the zoological order that includes monkeys, apes, lemurs, and humans.
A mammal, such as a kangaroo, whose young develop after birth, usually in a pouch.
An arthropod in zoology that typically has a hard outer shell and jointed legs, such as a crab, lobster, or shrimp.
An invertebrate animal in the zoological class Arachnida, typically with eight legs, such as a spider, scorpion, mite, or tick.
An invertebrate animal with a soft body, often protected by a shell, such as a snail, clam, or octopus.
In zoology, an animal that eats meat.
An animal that eats only plants.
An animal that eats both plant matter and other animals.
A bird, especially a perching bird, that produces a melodious call or song.
A bird that lives along the coast and feeds at sea.
A bird that hunts and feeds on other animals, such as an eagle or hawk.
An animal that does not have a backbone.
An animal in the phylum Chordata, a group that includes vertebrates and their close relatives.
An invertebrate animal in the phylum Arthropoda, characterized by jointed limbs and a hard external skeleton.
A terrestrial arthropod in the zoological group Myriapoda, with an elongated body and many legs, such as a centipede or millipede.
A crustacean in the zoological order Decapoda, typically having five pairs of walking legs, such as a crab, lobster, or shrimp.
An aquatic invertebrate in the zoological phylum Cnidaria, such as a jellyfish, coral, or sea anemone, characterized by stinging cells.
An invertebrate marine animal of the phylum Echinodermata, such as a starfish or sea urchin, typically with a spiny skin and radial symmetry.
A mollusc in zoology that has a shell made of two hinged parts, such as a clam or oyster.
A mollusc in the zoological class Gastropoda, such as a snail or slug.
A marine mollusc of the class Cephalopoda, such as an octopus, squid, or cuttlefish, with arms or tentacles around its head.
A segmented worm belonging to the phylum Annelida, such as an earthworm or leech.
A zoological term for a worm of the phylum Nematoda, typically with a slender, cylindrical, unsegmented body.
A vertebrate animal with four limbs, or descended from ancestors that had four limbs.
A marine mammal of the zoological order Cetacea, including whales, dolphins, and porpoises.
A marine mammal in the zoological group that includes seals, sea lions, and walruses.
A hoofed mammal, such as a horse, deer, or cow.
A hoofed mammal in zoology that regurgitates and rechews partially digested food, such as a cow or deer.
An egg-laying mammal, such as a platypus or echidna.
A mammal in the zoological order Lagomorpha, such as a rabbit, hare, or pika.
A member of the zoological family Hominidae, which includes humans and the great apes.
A bird of the order Passeriformes, which includes perching birds and most songbirds.
A marine mammal of the order Sirenia, such as a manatee or dugong.
A small aquatic invertebrate in the phylum Bryozoa that lives in colonies and is commonly called a moss animal.
An African burrowing mammal with a long snout that feeds mainly on ants and termites.
A medium-sized North American wild cat with tufted ears and a short tail.
A small South American rodent with very soft fur, belonging to the genus Chinchilla.
A wild dog native to Australia, often classified as a subspecies of the gray wolf.
A small rodent in the family Gliridae, typically with a bushy tail and known for hibernating.
In zoology, an ermine is a stoat (Mustela erminea) in its white winter coat.
A small, tailless ape with very long arms, adapted for swinging through trees in the forests of Southeast Asia.
A large African antelope of the genus *Connochaetes*, known for migrating in huge herds.
